name: Oregon

context: OR 589: Cross wind trap strips are herbaceous strips set across the most erosive wind on cropland where wind erosion is a concern.
OR 603: Herbaceous wind barriers are narrow strips of plants in the field that slow wind and cut erosion.
OR 609: Surface roughening is used where soils with a surface layer suited to clod formation have a high potential for wind erosion.
cover_rules: OR 340: Plant the cover crop as early as possible and terminate as late as practical (late vegetative stage or later) to maximize biomass.
OR 340: Do not burn cover crop residue; leave residues on the soil surface after termination.
OR 340: Use current erosion prediction technology to set the surface and canopy cover the cover crop must provide.
residue: OR 329: No-till keeps residue on the soil surface year around; crop interval STIR must be less than or equal to 20.
OR 345: Reduced till crop interval STIR must be no greater than 80; do not burn residues.
OR 345: Select tillage equipment that leaves enough aboveground residue during the periods with the highest erosion rates.
barriers: OR 603: Barriers have a minimum expected height of 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50 percent; spacing must not exceed 10 times barrier height.
OR 589: Trap strips are at least 15 feet wide when stubble is 1 foot or more in height, and at least 25 feet wide when under 1 foot.
OR 588: Cross wind ridges are spaced no more than four times ridge height, within 45 degrees of perpendicular to the wind; poor on sandy soils.
windbreak: OR 380: The protected zone on the leeward side of a windbreak is 10 times the maximum design height (H) of the tallest row.
OR 380: Select species adapted to soils and climate, and taller than the height of the crop; do not use species on invasive or noxious weed lists.
roughening: OR 609: Wide chisel spacing or skip-chiseling gives uniform clods; close, shallow spacing pulverizes soil and does not stop blowing.
OR 609: Begin roughening on the windward (upwind) edge of the field; treatment must reduce wind erosion by 25 percent.
OR 588: Crosswind ridges can be made as emergency tillage on bare fields but are temporary; on sandy soils make them when soil is moist.
grazing: OR 528: Plan grazing to keep ground cover from canopy, litter and trampled residue that protects the soil from wind and water.
OR 528: Minimize animal impact on areas with high soil erosion potential.
drought: OR 528: Write contingencies for drought, flood, wildfire and extreme weather; when conditions are not appropriate, follow the plan to avoid new concerns.
seeding: OR 550: Seeding rates are calculated on a pure live seed (PLS) basis; species must give adequate cover to control wind and water erosion.
OR Guide: Rates are lbs PLS per acre for drilled seeding; double the rate if broadcast.
dont_seed: OR Guide: Do not use crested or Siberian wheatgrass on sites that receive > 12 inches mean annual ppt.
crp: OR 327: Conservation cover must keep the plant biomass and cover needed to reduce wind and water erosion; revegetate bare spots.
disturbed: OR 342: Critical area planting stabilizes areas with existing or expected high rates of soil erosion by wind or water.
OR 484: Mulching reduces wind erosion; anchor mulch with tackifiers, pinning, netting or crimping if needed.
dunes: OR 342: Dune plants must survive burial by blowing sand, sand blasting, salt spray and drought; use sand fences or brush matting.
OR Guide: Mammoth wildrye is long-lived on inland sand dunes; consider American dunegrass for dune stabilization.

shrubs.name: Rocky Mountain juniper
advice: OR Guide: Rocky Mountain juniper is a drought tolerant windbreak species needing 12 plus inches of annual precipitation.

shrubs.name: Eastern redcedar
advice: OR Guide: Eastern redcedar has some windbreak potential in Eastern Oregon; needs 15 inches plus annual precipitation.

shrubs.name: Bitterbrush
advice: OR Guide: Plant bitterbrush as seedlings or transplants at 3 ft spacing.

shrubs.name: Big sagebrush
advice: OR Guide: Plant big sagebrush as seedlings or transplants at 3 ft spacing.
